stories.summary: Nvidia warned of higher prices for servers containing its AI chips as soaring memory costs strain the AI buildout. Nvidia told some of its biggest customers to expect price hikes of more than 15%, Bloomberg reported, highlighting memory chip companies’ leverage over the AI industry. Nvidia is also pushing into AI, contributing to the squeeze: It will spend $6 billion to license technology from startup Poolside to build an open-weight model, competing with Chinese leaders DeepSeek and Moonshot and US companies OpenAI and Anthropic. That comes as frontier AI companies face pressure from open models. Anthropic’s US customers are increasingly using cheaper alternatives to its strongest models, raising questions about its high spending on advanced AI ahead of a potential record-breaking IPO. — Lauren Morganbesser

According to a Dakota County criminal complaint, the men were clearing branches Thursday when they began “f---ing around” with a hydraulic, truck-mounted grapple. Crimmins allegedly moved the machine to make its shadow appear to grab Lynch, but was watching the shadows rather than Lynch himself. He reportedly failed to realize the grapple was closing on Lynch’s actual head until it was too late. Police found Lynch “with a large amount of blood around his body and a significant injury to his head,” the Dakota County Attorney’s Office said. articles.summary: Carlos Perez Gallardo / REUTERS Police have reprimanded a father who left his “tired” seven-year-old son alone on Japan’s Mount Fuji for several hours while the family continued to hike. A worker spotted the boy sitting alone at a hut around 8,200 feet above sea level, which is over halfway up Japan’s tallest mountain, on Thursday and called the police. Authorities said the boy was hiking with his father and older brother, and was told to “wait here” at the hut when he became “tired” and did not want to hike any further. Japanese network TV Asahi said the boy was left with snacks, a soft drink and no money. When the father and his other son returned after five hours of hiking, police were waiting with the boy, who was unharmed and was handed back to his father. Officers warned the dad he could be held criminally liable, and he expressed remorse. Two men died last month while climbing Mount Fuji.
